data.name: Sarvajit
data.gender_notes: Sarvajit is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Sanskrit, Sarvajit means 'one who wins over all' or 'victorious in all battles'. The name Sarvajit carries the meaning “Victorious in all battles” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Sarvajit usually hope their child will grow to embody victorious in all battles and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Sarvajit belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Victorious in all battles.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sarvajit total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sarvajit carries a significant cultural impact as it highlights the Hindu belief in achieving success and victory in all aspects of life - personal and professional. It also represents bravery, resilience, and the unwavering determination to overcome challenges and obstacles. This name is often considered an aspirational one, inspiring individuals to strive for excellence in their pursuits.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Sarvajit holds tremendous significance as it underscores the essence of 'oneness with the divine' and 'being victorious over the inner self'. The name reminds us of the importance of achieving inner peace and enlightenment, as true empowerment lies within. It invokes the sense of surrender to the divine will and the grace that comes with such surrender. By embodying the qualities of a Sarvajit, one is said to have achieved victory not only in the material world but also in the spiritual realm, leading to a fulfilling and purpose-driven life.

historical_references.reference: Sarvajit was a famous Hindu warrior belonging to the Yadava clan, who is mentioned in the Mahabharata. He was a close friend and ally of Krishna, and fought on the side of the Pandava forces during the Mahabharata war.
historical_references.context: Ancient India, Mahabharata war, Hindu mythology, Yadava clan, Krishna's friend and ally

historical_references.reference: Another Sarvajit, a Jain monk from the 5th century CE, is known for his philosophical works, particularly his commentary on the Tattvartha Sutra. He was an influential figure in Jainism and is considered an important scholarly figure in Indian history.
historical_references.context: Ancient India, Jainism, philosophical works, Tattvartha Sutra commentary, influential figure in Indian history

On LinkedIn, it is a popular name among professionals, signifying success in all areas of life. On Instagram, it is a trending name for newborns, reflecting the parents' hopes and dreams for their child's future success and happiness.
